svg.title: HDLC PCB wiring, ESP32-S2 Mini and MAX3490E
svg.text: RC422Dev HDLC: ESP32-S2 board, 2 x MAX3490E, plugs straight into the ND (ND manual pin numbers)
Green = TX (board to ND), blue = RX (ND to board), orange = jumper wire. Powered from the USB cable. Amber tags [A1]... mark assumptions (listed at the bottom).
DATA chip U1: board to ND
DATA chip U1: ND to board
CLOCK chip U2: board to ND
USB cable to the laptop = power + serial
ground, common with the DB-25 pin 8
to GND (same ground as chips and ESP)

- MAX3490 pins (VCC 1, RO 2, DI 3, GND 4, Y 5, Z 6, B 7, A 8), supply 3.0 to 3.6 V, no enable pins, Y non-inverting, Z inverting: MAX3483-MAX3491 datasheet pages 7 and 8 (Figure 2) and page 12 (function tables).
The repo copy docs/MAX3483-MAX3491.pdf has only two pages; the full datasheet was downloaded to read the pin table.

- ND pins, from the ND manual (sections 2-20 page 7 and 2-22 page 5): the ND OUTPUTS data on 14 (+) and 2 (-) and clock on 3 (+) and 15 (-); it takes INPUT data on 16 (+) and 4 (-) and clock on 18 (+) and 6 (-).

- ESP32-S2 Mini pins: handoff note 2026-11-08 (a working test against the Pico): TX data GPIO 11, TX clock GPIO 7, RX data GPIO 9, RX clock GPIO 12, 3.3 V logic straight, 19200 bit/s, 25 ns input glitch filter on the two inputs.
- Old breadboard wiring, converted to the ND's numbers because your cable was flipped: drivers on 16/4 and 18/6, receivers on 14/2 and 15/3, plus the four jumpers.
[A1] The conversion from your printed numbers to the ND's numbers comes from your jumper beeps, not from a pin-by-pin test of the flipped cable.
[A2] The S2 Mini's 3V3 pin can feed two MAX3490 (a few milliamps) and its 5V pin is the USB 5 V. Both are NOT checked against the board's schematic. The 5V pin is not used here.
[A3] The ND's socket is female, so the PCB needs a MALE DB-25 plug. This is Ronny's statement, not checked on the machine.
[A4] Receive clock: A on pin 15, B on pin 3, copied from the old wiring. It is not proven that a real ND needs this.

[A5] The jumpers (3-5, 15-17, 11-24-23, 22-10) are what the 3015 card's cable plug has. 5 and 17 are also the MEGALINK busy-input pins, so this board suits the 3015 only. Not verified that the ND needs them.
Put them on solder jumpers so they can be removed.
[A6] Not drawn: line termination (120 ohm), surge protection, USB connector details. The firmware for the ESP32 is in its own project, not in this repo (the Pico PIO code here is not used).
Chips: MAX3490E, 3.3 V, full duplex, no enable pins (datasheet). Through-hole PDIP-8 is MAX3490EEPA, SOIC-8 is MAX3490EESA (your RS422_3v3_Transceivers.md).
Target speed: at most 307.2 kbps (MEGALINK 983 kbps and busy not supported). The MAX3490 is rated 10 Mbps.
